column1: # THE NINE ACTIVE PRODUCTION POLYC PARSER DECISION SITES.
# Each authority is proved at FOUR levels:
#   1. the SELECTOR is ON for it in the qualified production build;
#   2. the CALLER object carries an UNDEFINED IMPORT of its symbol;
#   3. the CALLER object carries NO local definition of it;
#   4. the LINKED binary carries EXACTLY ONE definition of it, and
#      the caller's function-scoped relocation table places a real
#      relocation to it inside the caller's own function range.
# THE NINTH AUTHORITY -- NEW IN THIS ACT
# THE MEASURED SYMBOL TABLE IN THE LINKED PRODUCTION BINARY
# THE MEASURED IMPORT TABLE IN THE CALLER OBJECTS
COMMAND=for o in build/CMakeFiles/hcc.dir/*.o; do nm "$o" | grep ' U _Bootstrap'; done
# THE MEASURED DEFINITION TABLE IN THE POLYC SUBJECT OBJECTS
COMMAND=for o in build/parser-*-subject.o; do nm "$o" | grep -E ' T _Bootstrap'; done
# NINE subject objects, NINE definitions, NINE distinct symbols.
# NO C OBJECT DEFINES ANY OF THE NINE SYMBOLS.  Every definition is in
#   The legacy C keyword chain is COMPILED OUT of the ON path: the
#   selector-OFF object carries ZERO references to the successor, and
#   the ON object's function-scoped relocation table shows the decision
#   leaving the function through the PolyC symbol, not through a
#   keyword comparison.  The legacy chain survives ONLY in the
#   selector-OFF object, which is the G0 oracle.
#   The tracked source delta is exactly: src/parser.c (the SUB-004
#   seam and its adjacent oracle wrapper), src/CMakeLists.txt (the
#   subject option, production and link wiring), Makefile (the
#   subject producer, prerequisite edge and the generation rules),
#   and the new PolyC component.  No other src/** file, no existing
